headline: Southborough advanced a $38 million Neary School renovation plan, prepared tight FY28 operating budgets, and adopted a competitive municipal salary benchmark.
synopsis: In October, town boards confronted major long-term capital and operating budget questions ahead of the upcoming fiscal year. The Elementary School Building Committee advanced a comprehensive $38 million addition-renovation design for Margaret A. Neary Elementary School after determining a $15 million scope could not cover essential repairs. Meanwhile, municipal and school officials began assembling FY28 budgets under tight Proposition 2 1/2 constraints, evaluating level-funded cut scenarios and potential operating overrides. Town boards also prepared for Special Town Meeting, reviewing articles for trail bridge funding, landfill water connections, and borrowing rescissions. In addition, the Personnel Board endorsed the 60th percentile salary benchmark for town staff, and regulatory reviews progressed for the proposed Costco project on Coslin Drive.

top_items.title: Neary School $38 Million Renovation Advances to Schematic Design
top_items.why: Architects reported a $15 million upgrade would leave only $5.8 million for direct construction after required code updates, failing to fix core mechanical systems. The committee voted unanimously to advance Option 3, a comprehensive addition and renovation, to schematic design.
top_items.body: Tappé Architects presented an analysis showing that soft costs, contingencies, and mandatory building code upgrades would consume most of an austere $15 million budget, leaving heating, ventilation, and educational needs unmet without qualifying for state reimbursement. The Elementary School Building Committee voted 4-0 on October 21 to move forward with schematic design and detailed cost estimates for Option 3. School and capital committees are coordinating joint sessions with the Select Board and Advisory Committee to evaluate municipal borrowing capacity.

top_items.title: Personnel Board Adopts 60th Percentile Salary Benchmark
top_items.why: The Personnel Board voted unanimously to set municipal salary schedules at the 60th percentile of 18 peer communities, expanding from 9 to 12 grades. An appeals panel was created with a November 24 deadline following employee feedback on specific job classifications.
top_items.body: Consultant MGT presented findings covering non-union Salary Administration Plan positions, showing five roles currently paid below proposed minimums and one above the maximum. Several department heads objected to proposed job groupings, notably under the broad Business Administrator title. The board approved the 60th percentile benchmark and established a three-member review panel to evaluate employee appeals before Town Meeting warrant preparation.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail Footbridge CPA Funding Advanced to Town Meeting
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to send the $217,318 supplemental CPA funding request for the Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge to Special Town Meeting without floor cuts. The Trails Committee prepared voter outreach and pursued matching state grant opportunities.
top_items.body: Facing unfavorable recommendations from the Select Board and Advisory Committee, the Trails Committee and Community Preservation Committee debated whether to reduce the funding article through a floor amendment. The CPC voted 3-2 to retain the full article on the warrant to avoid floor confusion, bringing total project funding to $428,550. The Trails Committee finalized informational materials and began preparing an application for a state MassTrails grant of up to $100,000 to offset town costs.

top_items.title: Costco Warehouse Wetland and Stormwater Plans Presented
top_items.why: Costco presented environmental and stormwater plans to the Conservation Commission for a 167,000-square-foot warehouse and 30-fuel-pump station at 21 Coslin Drive. Concurrent reviews before the Conservation Commission and Planning Board were continued into November.
top_items.body: Representatives for Costco Wholesale detailed site plans to redevelop the former Dell EMC office parcel straddling Southborough and Westborough, including hydrodynamic separators and constructed wetland basins. The Planning Board extended its decision deadline to December 18 and scheduled a special hearing for November 2 to review pending traffic peer reviews, while the Conservation Commission continued its hearing pending state and peer review comments.

top_items.title: Town and Schools Prepare Dual FY28 Budget Scenarios
top_items.why: Departments began modeling level-service and level-funded budget scenarios amid tight Proposition 2 1/2 tax levy limits and potential override discussions. Regional school officials also projected approximately $600,000 in potential savings from employee health insurance restructuring.
top_items.body: Municipal departments and local school committees received instructions to build two FY28 budget tracks: one maintaining services assuming override funding and another cutting positions and operations if an override is not pursued or fails. The Regional School Committee examined five FY28 capital projects totaling $460,000 alongside an anticipated $800,000 drop in regional debt service, while negotiating health plan deductible alignments to reduce future operating costs.

top_items.title: School Committee Approves Unit A Teacher Contract Amendments
top_items.why: The Southborough School Committee voted 5-0 to amend the Unit A collective bargaining agreement, revising retirement incentives and aligning local teacher pay with Algonquin Regional High School starting July 1, 2027.
top_items.body: Following executive session deliberations, the School Committee reconvened to approve updates to Articles 22 and 29 of the contract with the Southborough Teachers Association. The amendments adjust the district retirement incentive program and transition Southborough elementary and middle school teacher salary scales to match Algonquin's regional schedule starting in FY28.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee Recommends Water Line to Protect Homes
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Article 7 at Special Town Meeting, which allocates $240,000 from water retained earnings to connect two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill to town water.
top_items.body: The Advisory Committee clarified that the town will pay the full cost of extending the water main and connecting the two residences from the street into the homes. The measure addresses contamination risks after chemical detections in nearby monitoring wells, allowing the town to eliminate perpetual state-mandated private well testing.
